title: A look at Bazel and where it shows up

videos.script: You have built the ISBN checker twice now. Once with Maven, once with Gradle. {{two-builds}} This lesson builds it a third time, with Bazel. It is a short lesson, and it asks two questions: where will you meet Bazel, and why does it exist? {{why}} Bazel came out of Google. There it builds one enormous repository, in many languages, for thousands of engineers. {{monorepo}} Its idea fits in a few words. Every step of the build declares all of its inputs. So each result can be found again by a hash of those inputs, on your machine or on a colleague's. {{cache}} You will install Bazel through its launcher, write a module file and two BUILD files, and then build, run and test the checker. {{build}} Then you will weigh the cost. For five developers with one service, Bazel is the wrong tool. For two hundred developers in one repository, it can be the right one. {{trade}}
